value.text:
The University of Southern California (USC) is a private nonprofit research university in Los Angeles, California. Its main University Park campus is southwest of downtown Los Angeles, while a separate Health Sciences campus supports medical education and biomedical research. The institution also operates other sites, including a Capital Campus in Washington, D.C. Its roots date to 1880, when Robert Maclay Widney helped arrange land and financial support for its establishment. The university opened that year with 53 students and ten faculty members. Although initially associated with Methodism, it ended its formal church ties in 1952.

USC's organization includes the Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences, a graduate school, and professional schools spanning engineering, medicine, cinema, architecture, law, education and other fields. The university's teaching and research extend across the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences and professional disciplines. The Health Sciences campus hosts clinical and biomedical programs, including cancer and neuroscience research.

Its published figures require date-specific interpretation. The English Wikipedia infobox records 47,147 students for 2024, including 21,023 undergraduates and 26,124 postgraduates, while a separately dated 2025–26 account reports roughly 45,815 enrolled students. The infobox gives a 2023–24 budget of approximately US$7.4 billion and a 2025 endowment of approximately US$8.8 billion. These are different financial measures, not interchangeable indicators of current spending or assets.
